pool.text: Under Archbishop Byzantius, Bari attached to the see of Rome and received provincial status.
Robert Guiscard captured Bari after a three-year siege, ending Byzantine power.
Relics of Saint Nicholas arrived in Bari and were installed inside the basilica.
Peter the Hermit preached the First Crusade within the city of Bari.
Urban II convened the Council of Bari to reconcile Eastern and Western churches.
Holy Roman Emperor Lothair captured the city of Bari successfully.
A Byzantine army seized control of Bari away from William I of Sicily.
A combined German and Hungarian army besieged and captured Bari during conflict.
Princess Bona Sforza of Aragon left Poland and settled in Bari.
Princess Bona Sforza passed away within the city of Bari.
Joachim Murat began a new urbanization process, setting a chessboard growth model.
Modern plumbing arrived as the first completed leg of the Apulian Aqueduct.
The British 1st Airborne Division took Bari without facing any resistance.
German Luftwaffe bombers attacked Allied forces and shipping in the port.
The Liberty ship Charles Henderson exploded in the harbour while offloading aerial bombs.
The city of Bari was divided into five distinct municipalities called Municipi.
Immigrants accounted for a total of 6.0 percent of the population.
